nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$ and a subset $A$ of $\{0, 1, \dots, n-1\}$, the binary code of $A$ is the natural number $b(A) = \sum_{i \in A} 2^i$.
nodes.title: Binary code of a subset

nodes.summary: For a family $U$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the string $s(U)$ is the list of the sort keys of the nonempty members of $U$, in increasing order.
nodes.title: String of a family

nodes.summary: A family $U$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is canonical, the canonical representative of its isomorphism class, if for every permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ the string $s(U)$ is lexicographically at most the string $s(\sigma(U))$ of the permuted family $\sigma(U)$.
nodes.title: Canonical family

nodes.summary: A family $U$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is union-closed if $A \cup B \in U$ for all $A, B \in U$.
nodes.title: Union-closed family

nodes.summary: Let $A_1, \dots, A_k$ be nonempty subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $A_i < A_j$ in the set order whenever $i < j$, and suppose the family $U = \{\emptyset, A_1, \dots, A_k\}$ is canonical. Then for every $m \le k$, including $m = 0$, the family $\{\emptyset, A_1, \dots, A_m\}$ is canonical.
nodes.title: Prefixes of a sorted canonical family are canonical

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $k$ and $m$ be natural numbers with $1 \le m \le k$, and let $A_1, \dots, A_k$ be nonempty subsets of $\Omega_n = \{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $A_i < A_j$ in the set order whenever $i < j$. Suppose the family $U = \{\emptyset, A_1, \dots, A_k\}$ is union-closed, every element of $\Omega_n$ lies in some member of $U$, $U \ne \{\Omega_n, \emptyset\}$, and $U$ is canonical. Then the prefix family…
nodes.title: Orderly generation of union-closed families

nodes.summary: For a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and a family $U$ of subsets of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the permuted image $\sigma(U)$ is the family $\{\sigma(A) : A \in U\}$, where $\sigma(A) = \{\sigma(a) : a \in A\}$.
nodes.title: Permuted image of a family

nodes.summary: For a subset $A$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the sort key of $A$ is the natural number $(n - |A|) \cdot 2^n + b(A)$, where $b(A) = \sum_{i \in A} 2^i$ is the binary code of $A$.
nodes.title: Sort key of a subset

nodes.summary: For all subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, $A < B$ in the set order if and only if the sort key of $A$ is less than the sort key of $B$.
nodes.title: The sort key encodes the set order

nodes.summary: For subsets $A$ and $B$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$, $A$ precedes $B$ in the set order, written $A < B$, if $|A| > |B|$, or $|A| = |B|$ and $b(A) < b(B)$, where $b(A) = \sum_{i \in A} 2^i$ is the binary code of $A$.
nodes.title: Set order

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
